What is the TPP and why is it a good/bad thing?

Its an international trade treaty being written, the specifics of which are subject of a lot of rumor and speculation.

The general goal is to provide a level playing field for corporations between different countries. So that governments can't enact policies that favor local businesses. According to Reddit(and probably Voat) it will lead to the megacorporations ruling society and the end of democracy.

Its hard to say if its a good or bad thing as the treaty hasn't been finished yet. Once negotiations are finished, the treaties will be available for everyone to see.
There have been some drafts leaked on wikileaks, from what we've seen of them it's pretty bad.

I am going to copy/paste my explaination from [/v/outoftheloop](/v/outoftheloop) here:

The TPP is a trade pact with 11 Pacific rim countries. According to the US Trade Representative, they are Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, and Vietnam (note that China is not on the list).

People in favor of the TPP say it will liberalize trade in the region, lowering tariffs so companies can trade more freely and efficiently, raising GDP. What makes the TPP particularly attractive is the inclusion of Japan, who we have no trade agreement with yet.

Personally, I like free trade, but I hate the TPP, because it is not about free trade. Only 5 of the 29 chapters of the TPP is about trade at all, and the parts about trade are about propping up monopolies rather than extending more efficient, free trade around the region. Most of the TPP is about setting up an international court system staffed by corporate employees, who are not accountable to any democratic process. It also has much more strict anti-piracy laws so corporations can sue you for just about anything.

What Obama asked congress to do was to give him fast track authority. Fast track basically means that Congress gives up their line item veto power over treaties the president negotiates. Without fast track nobody will negotiate with the president in good faith, because they know congress will not let him do what he says he will do. If Obama didn't have fast track, he could be running back and forth between a dysfunctional congress and foreign nations to amend agreements forever, until the agreements fail when everybody gets frustrated. With fast track, the president gets foreign countries to agree to the treaty then congress gives it an up or down vote and if it passes it becomes law.

All the information we have on the TPP is from leaks, because the treaty is classified, which is unheard of for a major treaty that has been fast tracked to become law soon. It is so classified legislators can't read it. Even crazier, there are parts of it that will be classified for up to 4 years after the treaty goes into effect. If you want to read everything we have on it so far you have to read it on Wikileaks.

I'm very new to voat and I hope this sub becomes more than just somewhere to bash religious zealots. I'd like to see more of a personal touch in our posts so that's why I'm writing this. In hopes that we don't fall into the same trappings of the old r/atheism.

So, onto my opinion and a bit of my personal loss of faith.

When I was a boy I was raised Presbyterian and I remember the first concept I had of God. He was all around and he was good, guiding and helping people in need. He was more like a superhero in my mind but he was also a judge who perfectly knew and understood the thoughts and actions of all men. He would reward those who were good and punish the truly evil. I could accept this very easily and believed in that idea of God.

However, the older I became and the more of Christian mythology I learned the more I questioned. This is a familiar and relatable story for many of us atheists raised in religion. When I was young I questioned details of stories, such as the mountains and other inanimate objects bowing before the lord, did that mean that spirits of these things were acknowledged by the Bible? As I became a teenager I began to question the morality and motivations behind the almighty itself. The actions of the old testament didn't line up to my original image of what God was or even should be and for years I struggled with this. I even talked with my pastor who generally gave me answers but many times they were not to my satisfaction. More adding mystery than explanation.

At the age of 16 I took a religions course at community college (I dual enrolled while in high school) after which I briefly became a Buddhist and then after realizing that it didn't make sense to just pick the version of reality that I liked best, I became a Deist. In truth I was just afraid to call my self the A-word. It wouldn't be until I was 19 or 20 that I was able to admit that I saw no proof of God or anything supernatural. I was content with my atheism for years and vocal about it... then life happened.

By life I mean hardship and pain and struggling. Worst of all was learning of the horrors of man; child rape, North Korea, wealthy-privilege, American horrors of war, the stories in the news which infuriate and depress. It was for years that I just wanted action, something to be done, and hated myself for not doing more. It wore on me and still does to this day. It becomes even harder to reconcile when you're trying to keep a family together. You can't be depressed about the world and raise a boy with anything more than cynicism in his heart. It was when things were worst for me, I was skipping meals so that my family could eat, working a part-time job for no money, in grad school and not doing as well as hoped, and taking on more debt than I liked, that I was able to admit something to myself that I still want to this day. I just wanted to know that there was someone out there that was looking out for me and recognized that I was a good man. I could say I believed but I wanted and for a moment I did pray. It wasn't a prayer as much as a making a call and showing my desire, just hoping that maybe something in the universe really did care for me. I knew it was to nothing, but I just hoped a bit.

To this day that I still keep this hope up. Not for a christian God or anything like that but... it's sort of like when I was just a boy and God was a superhero to me. That's what I wanted. So that all the pain and suffering of the innocent won't be just that, and yields some cosmic return. It doesn't mean I think it's there but I just wish it was. I've lost my family in the last year, due to several circumstances, I'm working a job I hate, and paying down debts that I will never really be able to escape. I had put my faith in my wife and son but now I go on for my son and do the best I can to support my ex though she doesn't love me anymore.

Despite how bad things have gotten... I still do not pray but I do want. It's not as good as belief I suppose but I still know that I'm not fooling myself and that's somewhat encouraging. So what do you think? Do you want like me for justice on the divine level and stop short of actual belief?
